---
title: "Lab · Compose a Pico (Greeting Capsule, steps 6–7)"
---

The lab for this lesson is the shared **Greeting Capsule** lab under
[`labs/greeting-capsule/`](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/). This
Module 4 lesson exercises **steps 6 and 7** of that lab, which cover
composing a minimal Pico and resolving its capability requirement by
hand.

## Why these two steps

Memo23 §9 step 4 ("Create the first lab") assigns one end-to-end
capsule lab to Part 2, and memo2 §4 D4 fixes the two course terms
used here:

- **Step 6 — Compose a minimal Pico and validate it.** Produces
  [`labs/greeting-capsule/solution/pico.yaml`](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/solution/pico.yaml)
  and runs the Pico-shape check against the repository's existing
  [`definitions/pico.yaml`](../../../../definitions/pico.yaml). This
  is the only Pico-shape contract the Academy ships today; no new
  Pico validator CLI is added.
- **Step 7 — Resolve the capability by hand.** Produces
  [`labs/greeting-capsule/solution/resolution.md`](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/solution/resolution.md)
  in the shape of upstream
  `fixtures/scenarios/resolve-greeting.yaml`. The reference resolver
  belongs to `open-engineering-capsule/source` (memo2 §1 D1, §4 D4)
  under memo2 §5 follow-up (b), which has not been published yet.
  The step records the hand resolution against the one installed
  provider — exactly as this lesson's [index](index.qmd) teaches.

Steps 1–5 (fetch, define, validate, implement, test) belong to
Modules 2 and 3; this Module 4 lesson relies on their artefacts
(`solution/capsule.yaml`, `solution/greeting.py`, the passing test
suite) but does not re-run them.

## What you will produce (steps 6–7 only)

- A minimal composing Pico at `solution/pico.yaml` that declares one
  capability requirement, `oe.greeting@0.1.0`, under
  `spec.capabilities`.
- A `valid` print from the Pico-shape check (Step 6).
- A hand resolution report at `solution/resolution.md` whose
  `outcome` / `resolution` block is byte-equivalent to the upstream
  `fixtures/scenarios/resolve-greeting.yaml` `expected:` block at
  pinned commit `bf071c2c1b57`.

## What this lab does *not* do

- **No Academy resolver.** The lab records the hand resolution; it
  does not ship or invoke a resolver (memo2 §4 D4 Consequences for
  the Academy; memo2 §5 follow-up (b) is pending).
- **No fork of the upstream schema or scenarios.** `build/upstream/`
  is populated by `solution/fetch-upstream.sh` and is listed in the
  lab-local `.gitignore`; nothing under it is committed (memo23 §3.2
  / memo26 §5).
- **No new Pico validator CLI.** Step 6 uses the repository's
  existing `definitions/pico.yaml` via a short Python one-liner. The
  Academy adds no dedicated validator in this lesson.

## Verification quoted from the lab

Step 6 — expected output `valid`:

```bash
cd labs/greeting-capsule
python3 -c 'import yaml, jsonschema; d=yaml.safe_load(open("../../definitions/pico.yaml")); jsonschema.validate(yaml.safe_load(open("solution/pico.yaml")), d["spec"]["schema"]); print("valid")'
```

Step 7 — compare the `outcome` / `resolution` block in
`solution/resolution.md` against the `expected:` block of
`build/upstream/fixtures/scenarios/resolve-greeting.yaml`. They
should be byte-equivalent.
